explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM evaluators against human evaluation by calculating fine-grained correlation between their scores on the same 100 samples across both short-term and long-term feedback dimensions

prompts.notes: Full instructions and evaluation criteria provided for both turn-level (fluency, relevance, diversity) and dialogue-level (engagement, coherence, informativeness) evaluations with detailed definitions and scoring rubrics

guidelines.notes: Human evaluators used same quality dimensions as LLM judges, with assessment questions consistent with quality descriptions in Appendix A, using 1-3 scale (poor, normal, good)

sample_size.notes: Used 100 randomly sampled responses from DailyDialog dataset that were evaluated by both human and LLM judges

quantitative_scores.notes: Paper states 'the two types of feedback has significant correlation with human evaluation' but does not provide exact correlation coefficients
Same 100 samples used for both short-term and long-term feedback validation

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM evaluators (GPT-4) show significant correlation with human evaluation across all six quality dimensions, validating that automatic evaluators can provide effective feedback comparable to human judgments despite individual differences in open-domain conversation evaluation.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM and human evaluation assess identical six quality dimensions: three turn-level (fluency, relevance, diversity) and three dialogue-level (engagement, coherence, informativeness)
